title: Gui Architecture Mismatch
definition: A concept that refers to the incompatibility of a particular Graphical User Interface (GUI) architecture with a system's underlying hardware or software capabilities.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine trying to use a video game designed for high-performance computers on a slower laptop. Even though the game looks great, it might not run smoothly or perform as expected because it was built for a different system.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: In this context, NiceGUI, a GUI library used for the project, relies on persistent websockets for real-time updates. However, on CPU-only systems with slow LLM inference times, the websocket connection might idle out and drop, causing the entire UI to fail. This is a fundamental mismatch of architecture.
difficulty_levels.expert: This concept highlights the need for a deep understanding of a system's limitations and the appropriate selection of architectural tools. It also underscores the importance of considering the trade-offs between elegance and functionality in software design. This mismatch not only affects the user experience but also has implications for scalability and maintainability of the system.

extra_fields.insight: The conversation revealed that the current GUI architecture (NiceGUI) is not compatible with the CPU-only slow inference of the LLM, leading to a poor user experience. This insight highlighted the need for a pivot to a more suitable GUI architecture.
